title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 24 (Hearings and written proceedings)

content.overview: Subject to party agreement, the tribunal decides whether to hold oral hearings or conduct proceedings on documents. Unless the parties agreed that no oral hearing shall be held, the tribunal shall hold oral hearings at an appropriate stage if a party so requests. Parties must receive sufficient advance notice of hearings and inspections. Materials supplied to the tribunal and expert or evidentiary documents relied on must be communicated to the other party.
content.glance: Tribunal chooses oral vs documents subject to agreement; oral hearing on request unless parties agreed otherwise; notice and disclosure duties apply.
content.study: Subject to agreement, the tribunal chooses oral or document proceedings. A party request triggers an oral hearing unless the parties agreed otherwise. Sufficient advance notice is required. Disclosure of materials and expert/evidentiary documents relied on is mandatory.

sections.heading: Oral or written proceedings
sections.body: Subject to agreement, the tribunal decides; oral hearing on request unless parties agreed otherwise.

sections.heading: Notice
sections.body: Sufficient advance notice of hearings and inspections.

sections.heading: Communication of materials
sections.body: Statements, documents, expert reports and evidentiary documents relied on must be communicated to the other party.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must the tribunal hold an oral hearing under section 24?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: When a party requests one at an appropriate stage, unless the parties have agreed that no oral hearing shall be held.

examTips: Oral hearing on request unless agreed otherwise; notice and disclosure.
